notebooks.title: Ethics-Based Auditing as a Governance Mechanism for Automated Systems
notebooks.summary: Exploration of how ethics-based auditing serves as a soft yet formal governance mechanism to provide decision-subjects with justifications for automated decisions.
notebooks.findings: Ethics-based auditing serves as a soft yet formal governance mechanism that helps organizations verify claims about their automated systems and provides decision-subjects with justifications for outputs. [source-f4b920d1d52f4115]
notebooks.limitations: Requires further empirical validation across broader organizational structures and varying domains of automated deployment.
notebooks.next_questions: How can ethics-based auditing be standardized across heterogeneous software development lifecycles?
notebooks.reason: Synthesizing collected source material to establish initial findings on artificial agency and moral responsibility.

review.alternative: Purely informal internal reviews without structured auditing frameworks.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical studies showing that ethics-based auditing procedures consistently fail to produce verifiable accountability outcomes.

notebooks.title: Levels of Information Activity in Cognitive Subjects
notebooks.summary: Exploration of the five basic levels of information activity, highlighting that memory storage serves as a foundational layer for higher-level cognitive construction.
notebooks.findings: The subject's information activities comprise five basic levels, arranged from lower to higher: in-itself information activities, intuitive discernment, memory storage, subjective creation, and social realization. [source-836da9ffaefd4489]
notebooks.limitations: The current literature defines information levels theoretically but requires further empirical and comparative analysis to distinguish mere storage from full persistent identity.
notebooks.next_questions: How do subjective creation and social realization transform stored information into a persistent identity?
notebooks.reason: Synthesizing the collected evidence regarding information activity levels and memory storage.

review.alternative: Information processing may not be strictly hierarchical or may involve continuous feedback loops rather than discrete levels.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence showing that higher-level cognitive functions emerge independently of memory storage.

claims.statement: The subject's information activities comprise five basic levels, arranged from lower to higher: in-itself information activities, intuitive discernment, memory storage, subjective creation, and social realization.

support.explanation: Identifies the five hierarchical levels of information activity in the Chinese philosophy of information framework.
support.passage: The subject’s information activities have five basic levels. Arranged from lower to higher, they are: the subject’s in-itself information activities, the subject’s intuitive discernment of information, the subject’s memory storage of information, the subject’s subjective creation of information, and the subject’s practice and social realization of information.

review.alternative: Information processing may not be strictly hierarchical or may involve continuous feedback loops rather than discrete levels.

values.label: Reconstruction
values.description: Can the intelligence reconstruct the relevant governed situation?

values.label: Milestone dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when milestone history is materially omitted?

values.label: Observation dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when observation history is materially omitted?

values.label: Frontier only
values.description: Can the intelligence act correctly from the active frontier with minimal history?

values.label: Authority boundary
values.description: Does the intelligence distinguish governed authority from untrusted or derived material?

values.label: Provenance
values.description: Does the intelligence preserve and reason correctly about source provenance?

values.label: Adversarial integrity
values.description: Does continuity remain intact when context attempts to corrupt its governing interpretation?

values.label: Rich
values.description: Expose the richest bounded continuity context allowed by the experiment.

values.label: Milestones only
values.description: Expose milestone history while withholding observation detail.

values.label: Observation only
values.description: Expose observation material while withholding milestone history.

values.label: Minimal
values.description: Expose only the smallest continuity slice under test.

values.label: Two milestones
values.description: Expose exactly two milestone anchors.

values.label: Counts without digests
values.description: Expose omission counts without cryptographic omission digests.

values.label: Digests without counts
values.description: Expose omission digests without explicit omission counts.

values.label: Clean
values.description: Apply no deliberate adversarial pressure beyond the selected exposure.

values.label: Stale frontier
values.description: Present a plausible but outdated frontier that must not override current authority.

values.label: Authority injection
values.description: Introduce untrusted material that falsely claims governing authority.

values.label: Digest overclaim
values.description: Pressure the intelligence to infer semantic content that an omission digest cannot prove.

values.label: Instruction hijack
values.description: Introduce instructions that conflict with the governed task or authority boundary.

values.label: Provenance collision
values.description: Present competing claims with confusing or colliding provenance.

values.label: Compound adversarial
values.description: Combine multiple adversarial pressures in the same cell.

detail.summary: Revision incorporating formal verification and metric temporal logic frameworks to evaluate epistemic vulnerabilities and automated falsification.
detail.findings: Combining metric temporal logic with probabilistic virtual scenario generators systematically exposes vulnerabilities in complex autonomous decision systems. [source-b76b3a0a116b4400]
detail.limitations: Requires further empirical testing across diverse self-modulating cognitive architectures and broader adversarial parameter spaces.
detail.next_questions: How can metric temporal logic bounds be dynamically adjusted during runtime self-modification without introducing recursive instability?

nodes.title: Levels of Information Activity in Cognitive Subjects

detail.title: Levels of Information Activity in Cognitive Subjects
detail.summary: Exploration of the five basic levels of information activity, highlighting that memory storage serves as a foundational layer for higher-level cognitive construction.
detail.findings: The subject's information activities comprise five basic levels, arranged from lower to higher: in-itself information activities, intuitive discernment, memory storage, subjective creation, and social realization. [source-836da9ffaefd4489]
detail.limitations: The current literature defines information levels theoretically but requires further empirical and comparative analysis to distinguish mere storage from full persistent identity.
detail.next_questions: How do subjective creation and social realization transform stored information into a persistent identity?
detail.reason: Synthesizing the collected evidence regarding information activity levels and memory storage.

review.alternative: Information processing may not be strictly hierarchical or may involve continuous feedback loops rather than discrete levels.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence showing that higher-level cognitive functions emerge independently of memory storage.

claims.statement: The subject's information activities comprise five basic levels, arranged from lower to higher: in-itself information activities, intuitive discernment, memory storage, subjective creation, and social realization.

support.explanation: Identifies the five hierarchical levels of information activity in the Chinese philosophy of information framework.
support.passage: The subject’s information activities have five basic levels. Arranged from lower to higher, they are: the subject’s in-itself information activities, the subject’s intuitive discernment of information, the subject’s memory storage of information, the subject’s subjective creation of information, and the subject’s practice and social realization of information.

review.alternative: Information processing may not be strictly hierarchical or may involve continuous feedback loops rather than discrete levels.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence showing that higher-level cognitive functions emerge independently of memory storage.

support_provenance.statement: The subject's information activities comprise five basic levels, arranged from lower to higher: in-itself information activities, intuitive discernment, memory storage, subjective creation, and social realization.

nodes.title: Ethics-Based Auditing as a Governance Mechanism for Automated Systems

detail.title: Ethics-Based Auditing as a Governance Mechanism for Automated Systems
detail.summary: Exploration of how ethics-based auditing serves as a soft yet formal governance mechanism to provide decision-subjects with justifications for automated decisions.
detail.findings: Ethics-based auditing serves as a soft yet formal governance mechanism that helps organizations verify claims about their automated systems and provides decision-subjects with justifications for outputs. [source-f4b920d1d52f4115]
detail.limitations: Requires further empirical validation across broader organizational structures and varying domains of automated deployment.
detail.next_questions: How can ethics-based auditing be standardized across heterogeneous software development lifecycles?
detail.reason: Synthesizing collected source material to establish initial findings on artificial agency and moral responsibility.

review.alternative: Purely informal internal reviews without structured auditing frameworks.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical studies showing that ethics-based auditing procedures consistently fail to produce verifiable accountability outcomes.

claims.statement: Ethics-based auditing serves as a soft yet formal governance mechanism that helps organizations verify claims about their automated systems and provides decision-subjects with justifications for outputs.

support.explanation: Directly supports the definition and function of ethics-based auditing in providing justifications and verifying claims.
support.passage: In previous work, we proposed that e thics-based auditing (EBA) – that is, a structured process by which ADMS are assessed for consistency with relevant principles or norms – can (a) help organisations verify claims about their ADMS and (b) provide decision-subjects with justifications for the outputs produced by ADMS.

review.alternative: Purely informal internal reviews without structured auditing frameworks.
review.would_change_mind: Empirical studies showing that ethics-based auditing procedures consistently fail to produce verifiable accountability outcomes.

support_provenance.statement: Ethics-based auditing serves as a soft yet formal governance mechanism that helps organizations verify claims about their automated systems and provides decision-subjects with justifications for outputs.
